Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

for the projector decision, if campus technology confirms by october 3 that the auditorium projector has been repaired, we should keep the october 11 screening in the auditorium; if they do not confirm the repair by october 3, we should move that screening to room 214 in the library. those are the two branches, and neither should be described as already having happened. room 214 holds 74 people, compared with 160 in the auditorium, and it needs a separate key request through the library desk. the society has used it for small discussions, but not for a ticketed screening, so the room change would mean a smaller reservation limit and a different entrance note. if we move to room 214, we should also update the event page and printed signs by october 4, and we should not keep advertising the auditorium as the location. if the projector is confirmed repaired by october 3, none of those room-change steps are needed.

we have 38 members on the current mailing list, and the board expects around 90 people for borrowed light because last spring's mystery night drew 112. that estimate is not a promise about attendance, and it is not a reason to reserve more seats than a room can hold. the distributor allows us to admit nonmembers, but every guest still needs a ticket at the door. members will be able to reserve a free ticket until october 8; after that, any unclaimed member tickets can be offered to guests. the guest price is $4, payable by cash or campus card. we do not have permission to collect payments through the society's online form, so the form should only collect names and contact information. the treasurer, Nia Brooks, can bring the cash box and card reader, but she needs the final room choice before she checks out the reader.

there is also a file-delivery condition that affects the screening plan later. the distributor said the borrowed light file should arrive by october 7, but the society has not received it yet. if the file arrives by october 7, Jules can run the standard playback check on october 9; if it has not arrived by then, Jules should not test a substitute copy or use a personal streaming account. instead, Jules should contact the distributor and ask whether an authorized replacement file can be sent in time. we do not yet know whether a replacement would arrive before october 11, so the announcement should not promise that it will. the board can discuss rescheduling only if the distributor says there is no usable authorized file for that date. for now, the october 11 listing can stay up, but we should keep the file check on the agenda.

1. publicity and access
- Mara will revise the event page after the room decision, while Theo will prepare the two versions of the location line so we are not writing it from scratch at the last minute.
- if the screening stays in the auditorium, the entrance is through the south doors of the arts building; if it moves to room 214, guests should enter from the library courtyard and follow the temporary signs to the second floor. the library entrance locks at 8:00 p.m., so the door volunteer needs to arrive before then and remain at the courtyard entrance until doors close at 7:15.
- we should include that room 214 is on the second floor, and that the library elevator is available from the main lobby. the auditorium has step-free access from the south doors. please do not describe the library courtyard route as step-free, because we have not verified that route yet. Lea offered to call the access desk on october 2 and ask what route they recommend; until then the event page can simply say to contact the society with access questions.

for the october 25 screening, the quiet map has a separate discussion plan. the director's recorded introduction is six minutes long, and the distributor has approved playing it before the film. after the screening, we have reserved the seminar room across the hall from 9:15 to 10:00 for a discussion, provided the film ends by 9:05. if it runs later than 9:05, we should shorten the discussion so we leave the seminar room by 10:00; we cannot extend the reservation because another class uses it afterward. no one has asked the director to join remotely, and the society should not imply that she will attend. Malik can facilitate, and he plans to bring three questions about the film's use of recorded interviews. We have not decided whether to serve snacks, so the publicity copy should not mention refreshments.

we need a modest setup crew for both nights. On october 11, two people can check tickets, one can keep the entrance clear, and one can test the sound with Jules. If the event moves to room 214, we will need one additional volunteer to guide late arrivals from the courtyard, but that person should not be assigned unless the move happens. On october 25, the discussion room needs six chairs in a circle and a small table for the sign-in sheet; the seminar room's chairs are already there, so nobody needs to carry chairs from the auditorium. Theo has the society's folding sign, while Mara has the two battery lanterns used for the courtyard route last year. We should check their batteries on october 9, not assume they still work.

our spending limit for this series is $180, including printing and any room supplies. Printing the two posters and 40 small handouts is estimated at $32, based on the campus print shop's current prices. The library room has no rental charge for student groups, but the key request must be submitted at least three business days before the screening if that branch is needed. The society already has $96 in its event account, and the treasurer expects another $120 in membership dues by october 10. That incoming amount is expected, not received, so we should not commit to a purchase that depends on having it before it arrives. The campus card reader has no rental fee, although any card charges are deposited in the society account two business days later. Nia can report the final ticket total at the next board meeting rather than estimate revenue now.

at the october 1 board check-in, we should confirm who has the distributor contact, whether the technology team has given us a repair date, and whether Lea reached the access desk. We should also make sure the ticket form, guest-price line, and volunteer assignments match whichever room branch applies, without announcing a room change before the october 3 condition is known. If the projector is repaired by that date, keep the auditorium plan and remove the unused library directions from the public page; if it is not confirmed repaired, use room 214, submit the key request on time, and replace the location details by october 4. For the file, use the october 7 arrival check and the october 9 playback check as separate steps, and do not treat a distributor response as proof that the file has arrived.
